//VALIDATION: TWO LEVELS, and v2.1.259 hardened the outer one. ENTRY level (unchanged): an entry that fails schema validation — like these //-comment keys, if the schema rejects them — is STRIPPED with a warning and every remaining valid setting still applies, so the comments are safe to leave in and /doctor will mention them. FILE level (CHANGED v2.1.259): if this file, a managed-settings.d drop-in, an MDM plist, or an HKLM value is present but CANNOT BE PARSED AS A JSON OBJECT, Claude Code now REFUSES TO START and names the source (managed-settings.md: 'Claude Code refuses to start and prints an error naming the source, even when another admin source delivers a valid policy'). Before v2.1.259 a broken managed file could leave the policy silently unenforced. So: validate this file with `python3 -c "import json,sys;json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))" <path>` BEFORE placing it, or you brick every session on this machine until you fix or remove it. Stricter still for a policyHelper: any surviving schema violation fails the whole helper run and blocks startup. User/project/local settings behave differently again — a whole-file JSON/schema error raises a Settings Error dialog (fix / exit / continue-without) interactively and is skipped silently in -p runs; individually bad entries raise a Settings Warning and the rest of the file stays live.
